title: XRP Ledger’s Batch upgrade slips to Oct. 9 after validator support resets
summary: Title: Ripple news: XRP Ledger upgrade delayed 10 days after validators reset activation clock URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/09/26/xrp-ledger-s-batch-upgrade-slips-to-oct-9-after-validator-support-resets Published Time: 2026-09-26T04:30:00.000Z Markdown Content: Sep 26, 2026, 12:30 a.m. EDT 2 min read ![Image 1: Code on computer monitor (Markus Spiske/Unsplash)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Faf945cfdd3152f9ebc96d44f89ccafea550ccb57-5760x3840.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C300%2C5760%2C3240%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) XRP Ledger’s Batch upgrade slips to Oct. 9 after validator support resets. (Markus Spiske/Unsplash) Summary * The XRP Ledger’s Batch upgrade was delayed by at least 10 days after validator support briefly fell below the required threshold, putting its earliest activation at Oct. 9 if support holds. * Batch would allow users to submit up to eight transactions together, including all-or-nothing exchanges that could enable simultaneous payment and delivery of tokenized assets. * A separate upgrade allowing account owners to delegate specific tasks without sharing signing keys was also delayed and could activate as early as Oct. 8. An XRP Ledger upgrade expected to activate Sept. 29 has been pushed back by at least 10 days after validator support briefly fell below the level required to turn it on. The feature, called Batch, would let users submit up to eight transactions together. Its all-or-nothing option could let a buyer pay for a tokenized asset and receive it in one operation, preventing either side of the trade from completing alone. RippleX’s head of engineering, Ayo Akinyele, [previously told CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/09/19/ripple-says-asset-managers-are-preparing-for-xrp-ledger-s-next-payments-upgrade) that projects were being built around Batch and that Ripple would share more about work with asset managers once

summary: Title: Bitget's $352 million hack happened via spoofed transfers, not private keys, CEO Gracy Chen says URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/09/25/bitget-s-usd351-million-hack-happened-via-spoofed-transfers-not-private-keys-ceo-gray-chen-says Published Time: 2026-09-25T04:29:34.781Z Markdown Content: Updated Sep 25, 2026, 7:36 a.m. EDT Published Sep 25, 2026, 12:29 a.m. EDT 3 min read ![Image 1: Bitget's Gracy Chen. (Bitget live stream)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F78b3f87428f21c1dfdfb8cd5be86d655dc81ddb0-2994x1605.png%3Frect%3D71%2C0%2C2853%2C1605%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) Bitget's Gracy Chen. (Bitget live stream) Summary * Bitget lost $351.6 million after attackers compromised a wallet backend, spoofed transaction data and triggered the exchange’s authorization process, though the company said its private keys were not compromised. * The breach affected hot and warm wallets, but Bitget said its offline cold wallets remained secure and that it had stopped further unauthorized transfers. * Bitget said its $464 million-plus User Protection Fund would cover the loss, while deposits and trading remain open and withdrawals are suspended pending a security review. Crypto exchange Bitget lost $351.6 million in an overnight hack. CEO Gracy Chen said attackers faked transfer requests to drain funds but did not steal “private keys.” “The attacker compromised a critical backend system within our wallet infrastructure, used it to spoof transaction data, and triggered our authorization process to move funds out,” [Chen wrote on X](https://x.com/GracyBitget/status/2103284265563902056). “Private key compromise has been ruled out.” That distinction matters and points to a less alarming attack vector.
